input.title: purchase task allowance and current operator definitions
input.quote:
A completed purchase joins a distinct approved intent, an independently observed native transfer and complete useful output. Native transactions are counted once within each network. The cohort counts distinct accountable operator IDs whose reviewed deployment identifies an independent operator or customer, its buyer or merchant role, source basis, required network and operating or handed-over state. An operator’s agents and wallets share that identity; they do not create additional independent buyers. These are source-supported operator declarations, not automatic verification of corporate independence. Team-operated development purchases do not qualify. A returning buyer completes distinct intent groups on at least two UTC days. Reopening an acquired result or resuming its download continues the original purchase. Facilitators are also deduplicated by accountable operator for the same useful operation. [Original cohort operator guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/fcea2b04a19d9c14bbd337124ecdc83f5e36425c/stellar/scf_2026/sf47_budget_model/workspace/OPERATIONS-COHORT.md).

Cohort reporting includes completed/attempted purchases, complete/started parent datasets or files, returning buyers, accepted handovers and partial, unresolved, canceled and refunded outcomes. Required fulfillment remains separately visible. This makes the funded targets assessable against the whole observation window.
